protocol.policy: single-source cross-domain over three domains with Global (channel-wise) FiLM: train and select on one active source domain with its own code, then evaluate each of the other two active domains separately with no adaptation, every target image given the nearest source code (which has one candidate)

fold_membership.train: the source domain's budgeted stage-2 train partition
fold_membership.val: the source domain's budgeted stage-2 val partition
fold_membership.tests: each other active domain's budgeted stage-2 test partition, scored separately

protocol.source_test_rationale: Every sample keeps one project-wide role. The source domain's locked test partition is excluded rather than repurposed for training or validation, and target-domain validation images never influence checkpoint selection.
protocol.target_test_rationale: Each unseen target is capped to the common 50-image budget and reported separately, so target sample count is fixed without pooling acquisition domains
protocol.inactive_domains_note: RIM-ONE-DL is dropped from Step 4 for now. It stays under 'domains' so the locked parent and budgeted manifests, which cover all four domains, still revalidate; it is neither a source nor a scored target. The Stage 3 plain single-source runs already scored it and those columns are simply not read.
protocol.degeneracy_note: One source domain is one code. The FiLM generators receive a constant input, so the modulation is a fixed per-channel affine per encoder level, which InstanceNorm2d(affine=True) already provides; the nearest-domain selector has a single candidate and the fixed-code sweep a single entry. This arm is a control that must match the plain arm within seed noise, not a test of conditioning.
protocol.pairing_rationale: Paired with the existing Stage 3 plain single-source runs: same manifest, backbone, source images, budget, seeds, augmentation, optimiser and schedule; for each (source, target) the 50 target images are identical and the FiLM block is the only difference. Training on one domain does not depend on the other domains, so dropping RIM-ONE-DL does not require re-running plain.
protocol.test_conditioning_note: nearest_image, not nearest_domain: the per-domain rule decides one code per held-out domain from a single-domain test set and a reference sample, and this runner hands the engine the pooled union of two target domains. With one code the per-image and per-domain rules pick the same code for every image, so nothing is lost.

drishti_gs.note: provider_partition locks the 51-image provider test set and splits the 50-image provider training partition into 40 train / 10 val; test_fraction does not apply.

rim_one_dl.note: load_rim_one_dl_split_manifest is authoritative; the committed 70/10/20 manifest fixes membership and no fraction or seed in this file affects it.
